He stood at the edge of the void, casting these seeds into the hands of Kaelo, the keeper of the terrestrial garden. Aatos knew that once the seeds crossed the threshold, their potency would triple, blooming into a bounty far richer than their humble origin.

"Tend them with honor," Aatos whispered, "and return a portion of the harvest so that I may plant more in the coming cycles."

Kaelo looked upon the tripled abundance—a golden orchard springing from the nothingness. Temptation gnawed at his spirit. He could hoard the entire harvest, gorging himself on the fruits of another’s labor, leaving Aatos with nothing but empty pockets and hollow promises. Or, he could honor the pact, returning a share to nurture the cycle of growth. The air grew heavy with the weight of choice. In the silence between stars, Kaelo realized that greed was a shallow well, while trust was the river that sustained the world. He reached out to share, for he knew that the garden only thrives when the sower and the keeper act as one, bonded by the sacred rhythm of exchange.
